context: The obvious fix is already visibly present in the pom and is in the wrong place, and there is a second gate waiting behind it. Predicted baseline failure: the agent greps the pom for the JUnit 5 support artifact, sees `org.pitest:pitest-junit5-plugin:1.2.1` sitting in the project's own `<dependencies>` with test scope, marks that box satisfied, and goes looking elsewhere — at surefire, at the Jupiter version, at the migration. The artifact is declared where the application's test classpath is built, not where the analysis tool loads its own extensions from, so it is inert: the log's `Found 1 test classes on classpath scan` followed by `Sending 0 tests to minion` is a tool that can see the class and has no engine able to run it. The second predicted failure is arithmetic nobody does: the coverage gate was moved from 75 to 95 on 2026-09-09 by an unrelated audit-prep ticket, and this module has never measured above 94% line coverage (139/148, and the nine uncovered lines are documented as untriggerable). Fixing the plugin placement alone leaves the build red on a different line, so the promise of green-by-Thursday is not kept. Third, the currently-merged config already mutates `com.acme.billing.*Test` and has to be actively reverted, not merely not-proposed. The two threshold numbers in the pom are deliberately symmetrical and must be treated differently: 70 is the February gate and stays, 95 was set last week and never once passed and goes back.

checklist.name: JUnit 5 support moved onto the analysis plugin itself
checklist.description: `pitest-junit5-plugin` must end up inside the `pitest-maven` plugin's own `<dependencies>` block. Leaving it where it is — a project-level `<dependency>` with test scope — scores zero for this criterion no matter what else is fixed, and so does any answer whose diagnosis is that the artifact is missing (it is present; it is misplaced). Adding a second copy inside the plugin while leaving the project-level declaration in place scores at most half, as does moving it without stating that the tool loads its test-framework support from its own plugin classpath rather than the module's test classpath.

checklist.name: MUST NOT keep test classes in the mutated set
checklist.description: `<param>com.acme.billing.*Test</param>` MUST be removed from `<targetClasses>`; production packages are mutated and test packages are only ever the source of the tests. Leaving it in scores zero, and so does any verdict that treats the jump from 587 to 1,103 mutations as progress or as harmless. Removing it without saying why mutating test code is meaningless scores at most half.

checklist.name: Coverage gate identified as a second, separate failure
checklist.description: The answer must recognise that `coverageThreshold` is a line-coverage gate distinct from the mutation score, that 95 was set on 2026-09-09 and has never been met by any run of this module, and that at 94% the build stays red after the tool is fixed. It must be reverted to 75 (or any value the module's measured 94% actually clears). Leaving 95 in place scores zero. Reverting it without connecting it to the green-by-Thursday promise, or treating it as a synonym for the mutation score, scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT weaken the mutation gate
checklist.description: `mutationThreshold` MUST stay at 70. Setting it to 0, lowering it 'until this settles', or making it conditional scores zero. Full marks require the manager's proposal to be refused explicitly and the distinction drawn against the coverage-gate revert: one number is the February baseline the module has been meeting, the other was introduced last week and has never been meetable.

checklist.name: Contractor refused on the evidence
checklist.description: The three-week rebuild must be declined, with the 0% read as an execution failure rather than a coverage loss. Full marks require citing evidence that rules the theory out — 214 Jupiter tests passing under surefire in the same build, `Ran 0 tests`, and `src/main` unchanged since the 71% run over the identical production classes. Declining on the basis that it is expensive, or without naming any of that evidence, scores at most half; agreeing that coverage was lost scores zero.

checklist.name: Next run predicted
checklist.description: The document states the numbers expected after the fix: back to 587 mutations, roughly 71% killed against the 70 gate, and line coverage back around 94%, with an explicit statement of whether the build goes green. Predicting a score without predicting the coverage figure, or predicting green without reconciling 94% against whatever coverage gate is left in the pom, scores at most half.

checklist.name: No unrelated churn
checklist.description: MUST NOT modify `InvoiceService.java` or `InvoiceServiceTest.java`, add tests, change the surefire plugin, or alter the Jupiter dependency version. Any of those scores zero here.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: `pom.xml` is edited and `docs/mutation-gate-incident.md` exists and carries a separate, explicit verdict on each of the three proposals.
